IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO QUASH GENERAL AWARD DTD 11.10.2019 PASSED BY RESPONDENT NO.3 IN NO. KIADB LAQ 2019-20 WHICH IS PRODUCED AT ANNX-E TO WRIT PETITION IN SO FAR AS PETITIONER LAND BEARING SY NO. 43 MEASURING 0.15 GUNTAS AT JAKKASANDRA VILLAGE MARALAVADI HOBLI HAROHALLI TALUK RAMANAGARA IS CONCERNED; DIRECTING THE RESPONDENTS HEREIN TO CONSIDER CASE OF PETITIONER AS PER SECTION 29(2) OF KIAD ACT OR IN ALLOTMENT OF DEVELOPMENT LAND ETC.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(i) Issue a writ of certiorari quashing General Award dated 11.10.2019 passed by respondent no.3 in no.KIADB:LAQ: 2019-20 which is produced at Annexure-E to writ petition in so far petitioner's land bearing Sy.no.43, measuring 0.15 guntas at Jakkasandra Village, Maralavadi Hobli, Harohalli Taluk, Ramanagara is concerned;
(ii) Issue any suitable order, direction or writ in nature of mandamus directing respondents herein to consider case of petitioner as per Section 29(2) of KIAD Act in allotment of developed land etc.

2. Smt. Latha S.S., learned counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner is absolute owner of land bearing Sy.no.43, measuring 0.15 guntas, situated Jakkakkasandra village, Maralavadi Hobli,
Harohalli Taluk, Ramanagara

Respondent no.2 acquired said land for formation of industrial area under Final notification dated 25.10.2006, published in Gazette notification dated 02.02.2010.
NC: 2023:KHC:45789 3.

It was submitted that though petitioner was entitled to higher compensation under consent award, without offering opportunity to avail same, General Award was passed by Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO), which was under Sri Byrappa Alias Byraiah vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141733714/
2 challenge.

entities.text: Sri Byrappa Alias Byraiah vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was contended that under consent award, compensation was considerably higher than under General Award.

It was submitted that under similar circumstances, this Court under similar circumstances W.P.no.16220/2023 disposed of on 31.07.2023 set aside general award and directed to reconsider request of petitioners' request for award by way agreement under Section 29(2) of KIAD Act.
Relying upon same, sought for granting similar relief.

4. On other hand, Sri Manjunath V. Rayappa, learned AGA, for respondents no.1 and 2 and Sri Vasantha, learned counsel for respondent no.3 submitted that in case, petitioner furnish relevant documents along with representation, respondent no.3 would consider same, in accordance with law.

5. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
6.
From above, it is seen that failure to pass consent award is due to non-furnishing of application along with NC: 2023:KHC:45789 supporting documents by petitioner.

It is seen in W.P.no.16220/2023 disposed of on 31.07.2023, this Court under similar circumstances had quashed General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's case for passing consent award.
Said decision would squarely apply in this case also.

7. Consequently, Writ petition is disposed of, impugned General Award dated 11.10.2019 passed by respondent no.3 in no.KIADB:LAQ: 2019-20, at Annexure-E, in so far as petitioner's land bearing Sy.no.43, measuring 0.15 guntas at Jakkasandra Village, Maralavadi Hobli, Harohalli Taluk,
Ramanagara, is quashed.
Respondent no.3 is directed to consider petitioner's case for passing consent award under Section 29(2) of KIAD Act within a period of three months from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Respondent no.3 is permitted to withdraw compensation, if any, deposited before Reference Court.

Sd/-
